body.disclaimer: This is general guidance, not medical advice.

inputs.note: smoothed trend of 12 weigh-ins (v7); latest reading 82.6 kg
average of 12 days with steps in the last 14

targets.formula: Mifflin-St Jeor: 10 x 82.4 kg + 6.25 x 180 cm - 5 x 36 + 5 = 1,774 kcal.
targets.label: guideline

targets.formula: Resting energy 1,774 kcal x activity level 1.55 (8,400 steps a day on average, in the 7,500 to 9,999 band; the level inside the FAO/WHO/UNU 2004 range is our convention) = 2,750 kcal.
targets.label: convention

details.note: Wearable active calories are not used: reported errors are roughly 28 to 43% with no published correction.

targets.formula: Estimated from your logs: average logged intake 2,520 kcal minus the change in your weight trend (-0.9 kg over 21 days x 7,700 kcal per kg / 21 days) = 2,650 kcal, and logged intake is commonly under-reported.
targets.label: derivation

targets.formula: Maintenance 2,750 kcal (our step-band convention) - 0.5 kg a week x 7,700 kcal per kg / 7 days (550 kcal) = 2,200 kcal, rounded to 50 = 2,350 kcal.
targets.label: derivation

targets.formula: 2.0 g per kg x 82.4 kg = 164.8 g, rounded to 5 g.
targets.label: guideline

details.perMealTip: About 0.4 g/kg a meal, 33 g, across 4 meals.

targets.why: 1.6 g per kg of your 82.4 kg, to maintain muscle.

alternatives.label: 0.8 g per kg, the RDA for adults who do not train
1.4 g per kg, the low end of the range for training
2.0 g per kg, the top of the range for training

targets.formula: 28% of 2,350 kcal / 9 kcal per g = 73 g, never below 20%.
targets.label: guideline

targets.formula: Under 10% of 2,350 kcal / 9 kcal per g = 26 g.
targets.label: guideline

targets.formula: The remaining energy (2,350 - 4 x 165 - 9 x 73) kcal / 4 kcal per g = 258 g, never below 130 g.
targets.label: guideline

details.context: ACSM sport ranges: 3 to 5 g/kg for light activity, 5 to 7 g/kg for about an hour a day.

targets.formula: 14 g per 1,000 kcal x 2.35 = 33 g, for context the adequate intake for your age and sex is 38 g.
targets.label: guideline

targets.formula: Default 7 h 30 min within the 7 to 9 hours recommended for adults, and bedtime is wake time 7:00 AM - 7 h 30 min - 15 min of sleep onset = 11:15 PM (11:45 PM on days off).
targets.label: guideline

shortfall7.note: Information only; catch-up sleep has weak evidence, so there is no recovery plan.

regularity.advice: Keep sleep and wake times regular; there is no threshold.
regularity.note: Sleep Regularity Index (Phillips 2017) from your night records: 100 is perfectly regular. Only the 18:00 to 12:00 span each night record describes is compared.

targets.why: Adults need 7 to 9 hours, and 7 h 30 is the middle of that range.

alternatives.label: The low end of the recommended 7 to 9 hours
The top of the recommended 7 to 9 hours

targets.formula: 150 to 300 minutes of moderate or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous activity a week (a vigorous minute counts as two) plus muscle-strengthening on 2 or more days; this week you have 95 moderate-equivalent minutes and 1 strength days.
targets.label: guideline

details.note: No training-load ratio is used or prescribed.

targets.formula: 150 minutes of moderate activity a week (WHO 2020) spread over 7 days = 22 minutes a day, rounded up. The guideline is a weekly figure, so a rest day is fine as long as the week adds up.
targets.label: guideline
targets.why: WHO advises 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity a week. Spread over the week that is about 22 minutes a day.

alternatives.label: 300 min a week, the top of the WHO range

targets.formula: 7,000 steps a day, around where the benefit of walking starts to level off (5,000 to 7,000), raised in steps of 1,000 once you are above it.
targets.label: guideline
targets.why: Around where the benefit of walking starts to level off, 5,000 to 7,000 steps.

alternatives.label: The low end of where the benefit levels off for your age
The top of where the benefit levels off for your age

targets.formula: 3 sets x 18 reps, 75% (the middle of 70 to 80%) of your latest max of 24, a derivation from reps-in-reserve guidance rather than a published constant.
targets.label: derivation

targets.formula: Adequate intake of total water for men aged 19 and over is 3.7 L a day, and about 81% of it comes from drinking water and other drinks = 3.0 L.
targets.label: guideline

details.note: The Academies report that needs rise with activity and in heat; this is an adequate intake, not a requirement.

targets.why: The adequate intake of drinks for men, about 81% of total water. Needs rise with activity and heat.

alternatives.label: EFSA: 2.5 L of total water for men, the drinks part

targets.formula: WHO advises at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day, and one serving is 80 g (NHS 5 A Day), so 5 servings = 400 g.
targets.label: guideline

servingExamples: 1 medium apple, banana, pear or orange
details.note: Potatoes do not count, beans and pulses count once a day, and juice and smoothies count once however much you drink.

targets.why: WHO advises at least 400 g a day. One serving is 80 g, so 5 servings.

alternatives.label: 800 g, where risk was still falling (Aune 2017)
